answer: Socioeconomic status (SES) is the variable. In nested logistic regressions of BA degree completion (0/1, log-odds, N=8,773), the SES coefficient is strongly positive before academic controls — +0.473 for SES alone, +0.476 with sex, and +0.352 with race (White-reference) dummies added (the spec closest to the reported +0.3636) — and flips negative, ≈ −0.23, once BOTH race and academic characteristics are included (continuous ability+class-percentile coding: −0.2316, close to −0.2293; grouped quartile coding: −0.1593). The effect therefore falls from ~+0.36 to ~−0.23 and becomes statistically nonsignificant when academic characteristics are coded categorically (quartiles p=0.105; quintiles p=0.064); under continuous coding it is negative but only marginal (p=0.021) — spec-dependence reported plainly. Sex (~−0.20 throughout) and family size (~−0.48 throughout) never flip sign, confirming SES is the implicated variable. Mechanism (reversal): BA completion rises ~monotonically with SES tercile unconditionally (1.6%/2.9%/3.5%) but within high-ability students low-SES complete at 7.9% vs 5.7% for high-SES — SES is positively correlated with test score/class standing (r=0.46/0.30), which are the strong positive drivers of completion, so conditioning on ability/class rank (and race) absorbs SES's positive association and exposes a negative conditional SES–completion relation.

payload.hypothesis: Socioeconomic status (SES) is the variable whose effect on BA degree completion decreases from about +0.36 to about -0.23 and becomes statistically insignificant once race and academic characteristics (ASVAB test scores and class percentile) are controlled.
payload.workflow: Nested logistic regressions of BA DEGREE COMPLETED (0/1) on N=8,773 complete cases: reported SES coefficient across specs (SES only; +sex; +family; +sex+family; +race; +race+academic continuous/z-scored/quartile/quintile); negative controls (sex, family size — no sign flip); linear-probability robustness (HC3); mechanism confirmed via BA-rate table by ability x SES tercile.
